Best facet set of any agency: ?agency=<code>&state=All&topic=All&year=<yyyy>&page=N. agency=osec isolates the Office of the Secretary, which is exactly the Secretary-level subset this project wants; other codes (whd, osha, eta, ebsa) are sub-agencies. year= is a server-side date filter. The date is also encoded in the document URL (/newsroom/releases/osec/osec20260904). Rows carry no <time>. 403 to all HTTP clients; browser transport required. Confirms the pre-existing note that DOL publishes testimony on its own newsroom. ADAPTER WRITTEN 2026-09-08: 180 documents in the window, all dated. TWO SURVEY NOTES WERE WRONG. (1) `?agency=osec` does NOT filter - it returns a page with zero release links against twenty unfiltered; osec is a URL path segment, not a value that parameter takes. The listing is walked unfiltered and the sub-agency read from the path. (2) hrefs carry a leading AND trailing space inside the quotes, so a pattern anchored on href="/ matches nothing. Output is mostly sub-agency releases (ETA, OSHA, WHD, EBSA, MSHA, OWCP, ILAB) rather than the Secretary's; OFFICE_OF_THE_SECRETARY_ONLY in the module flips that, and the sub-agency is preserved in source_document_type either way (H-34).

UPDATE 2026-09-08: confirmed reachable from the project network - the PI opened /newsreleases/search successfully after completing an interactive human-verification step. That is the important qualifier: EPA does not merely fingerprint-block, it presents a CAPTCHA, so an automated browser will meet the same challenge and cannot pass it unattended. Two routes remain: a human solves the challenge once and the resulting session is reused, or the archive fallback already measured at 423 documents and 86% of business days (H-52). EPA is therefore the weakest of the three even though it is no longer 'blocked'. ADAPTER WRITTEN 2026-09-08 from the archived listing. Ordinary USWDS collection: 15 rows a page, ?page=N, a real <time> on every row. Only access is missing. Run it with scripts/desktop_harvest.py from a desktop session.
